C-STREAM-BUDGET.Summary: Enforce per-session resource budgets on the M-045 streaming document session — cumulative payload bytes, live section count and patch rate — so a legitimately paired, fully authorized extension can no longer push unbounded total volume, section counts or update frequency through /stream/*; every exceed is refused with an explicit budget-exceeded error while the session keeps its last valid revision.
C-STREAM-BUDGET.Problem: Security re-audit 2026-11-21 finding F-004 (no aggregate budget on streamed document content): after C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND (merged 55739a55) the stream routes authorize by the stored grant, but once authorized a single live session has no resource ceiling at all. In the observed live_server.rs the only cap in the file is HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SECS (live_server.rs:1467); handle_doc_open (live_server.rs:745) accepts any initial payload and any number of sections into LiveSession.sections (live_server.rs:73), and handle_doc_patch (live_server.rs:861) appends or replaces unlimited content on every accepted seq, then rebuilds the full document (rebuild_document_md), clones the full content and emits it to the frontend. Patch bodies arrive as axum Json extractions, where the framework's default per-request body limit bounds one request but nothing bounds the session aggregate: an append-heavy stream grows sections and document_md without limit, and per-patch rebuild/emit work grows with attacker-chosen volume and frequency. A paired extension — legitimately approved and holding the stream.document grant — can therefore exhaust memory and CPU of the host app through volume or rate alone. The refusal must be explicit: the session retains its last valid revision and the extension receives a budget-exceeded error it can handle — not a silent drop and not a kill without notice.
C-STREAM-BUDGET.Relationship: Continues the extension-host hardening line on the same module: C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH and C-SEC-STREAM-TABS fenced stream mutations by enabled identity, authorization generation and session owner/epoch; C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE scoped every incoming data route by manifest capability; C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING bound applies to a context-read document binding; C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND (merged 55739a55) authorizes the stream routes by the stored grant — grant_authorizes, authenticate_stream and the EXT_DOCUMENT_BINDINGS store are treated as present. This change is deliberately post-authorization resource governance: it constrains how much and how fast an authorized session may stream, not who may connect. The sibling findings from the same 2026-11-21 re-audit run are triaged separately and out of scope here.

Goals.Goal: A per-session cumulative payload byte budget, default 64 MiB (67108864 bytes) as a named constant (STREAM_BUDGET_TOTAL_BYTES): /stream/open counts the accepted initial document (the authoritative document_md bytes actually stored), each applied patch counts its content bytes, and a patch whose acceptance would push the cumulative total past the cap is refused with an explicit budget error and nothing is applied. The cumulative-volume model mirrors the audit finding — it bounds the total volume pushed through /stream/* and the resulting rebuild/emit work, and it cannot be cycled by replace-with-smaller-content traffic; held memory is bounded at the same figure because sections plus document_md never exceed the cumulative accepted volume.

A per-session live section count cap, default 4096 as a named constant (STREAM_BUDGET_MAX_SECTIONS), enforced at /stream/open on the post-dedup section list produced by build_sections_from_init; an over-cap open is refused with an explicit budget error and creates no session. Sections are fixed at open in the live-doc v2 data model, so the patch path needs no section-count check.

A per-session patch rate limit, default 30 patches per minute sustained with a burst allowance of 60 (named constants STREAM_BUDGET_RATE_PER_MINUTE and STREAM_BUDGET_RATE_BURST), implemented as a token bucket on the session refilling one token per 2 seconds and charged only on new in-sync patches — duplicates already short-circuit before validation and stay free. An exhausted bucket refuses the patch with an explicit budget error and leaves the session untouched. /stream/heartbeat and /stream/close stay budget-free: the heartbeat is the keepalive and carries no content. The bucket decision is extracted as a pure function in the module's existing pure-core style (alongside apply_section_patch and decide_open) so it is testable without real-time waits.

Each budget class logs its named marker in the file's BLOCK_* voice — BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_BYTES_EXCEEDED, BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_SECTIONS_EXCEEDED, BLOCK_STREAM_BUDGET_RATE_EXCEEDED — and the refusal rides the existing error JSON shape: a plain status code with a body of one "error" string naming the budget and the cap. No wire-format change: DocOpenResponse and DocPatchResponse keep their fields, and the extension distinguishes the refusal by status code and error text.

On every budget refusal the session keeps its last valid revision: revision, last_seq, document_md, sections and the emitted frontend state are untouched, the session stays active (never killed without notice), a subsequent heartbeat reports the unchanged revision, and the next valid in-budget patch on the same base_revision applies without needs_resync. Budget state lives on LiveSession and is replaced wholesale by a same-session resync re-open, keeping the documented resync recovery for a client that hit the cap honestly; cross-session accounting is out of scope.

tests.rs pins the budgets with the existing stream-fixture harness (incoming_fixture_caps plus direct handler calls): exceed-bytes, exceed-sections and exceed-rate each yield the explicit error with the last valid revision intact and no crash or reset; under-budget traffic behaves exactly as before; boundary values exactly at each cap pass.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact ObservedWriteScope: src-tauri/src/m045_ext/live_server.rs, its test module src-tauri/src/m045_ext/tests.rs and the M-045 graph record .grace/graph/features.xml only.

No wire-format change: budget refusals ride the existing one-error-string JSON response shape over ordinary status codes; the request/response struct fields of all /stream/* routes stay unchanged, so the renderer event stream (mt::live::update doc_open/doc_patch/doc_close payloads) is byte-compatible.

Grant semantics untouched: this change sits entirely after the capability/grant authorization gate; pairing, manifests, token issuance, revocation, disable fencing and the EXT_DOCUMENT_BINDINGS binding fence stay unchanged.

Session lifetime and binding semantics untouched: heartbeat timeout value and monitor, epoch and owner fencing, decide_open decisions, resync/replace-wholesale behavior and close semantics keep their current shape; budgets only add refusals and never close, expire or re-bind a session.
Budget state is process-local on the live session; no persistence, no config surface and no per-extension global accounting are introduced.
Keep repository artifacts English and synchronize the module contract CHANGE_SUMMARY and the graph SummaryDelta; no release publication.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Per-extension global quotas across sessions and persistence of budget state beyond the live session — a new session legitimately starts with fresh budgets.
Renderer UI beyond surfacing the existing error kind: the liveViewer bridge renders doc_open/patch/close only and has no error branch today, so it stays untouched.
Any change to the per-request body limit or to the /ext/* data routes (pair, text-insert, context, apply), including their budget-free behavior.
Mac App Store capability changes and release publication.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: An open whose accepted initial document exceeds the byte budget, or whose post-dedup section count exceeds 4096, is refused with the explicit budget error and creates no session; an open at exactly the cap succeeds, and the section-count refusal names the cap in its error.

A patch that would push the cumulative accepted payload bytes past 64 MiB is refused with the explicit budget error; the last valid revision survives: heartbeat still reports the previous revision, the session is still active, and the next valid in-budget patch on the same base_revision applies normally without needs_resync or any resync requirement.

A patch arriving with an exhausted rate bucket is refused with the explicit budget error and leaves revision, last_seq and document unchanged; a patch at the bucket boundary is accepted; duplicate retransmits do not consume the bucket.

Under-budget traffic behaves exactly as before the change: status codes, revision increments, duplicate and resync semantics, heartbeat responses and the emitted mt::live::update event sequence are unchanged on a normal patch session.
The stream_budget regression tests fail before the fix and pass after it, and the existing m045_ext suite stays green.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The new stream_budget tests — stream_budget_open_refuses_over_total_bytes, stream_budget_open_refuses_over_section_count, stream_budget_patch_refuses_over_cumulative_bytes, stream_budget_patch_refuses_over_rate, stream_budget_rejection_keeps_last_valid_revision, stream_budget_boundaries_at_exact_cap_pass, stream_budget_under_budget_traffic_unchanged — fail before the fix and pass after it; the existing m045_ext suite stays green; final GRACE assertions and current integrity pass.
